frames.narration: Three replicas, each holding the item at version 1. The settings are N = 3, W = 2 and R = 2. Note that R + W = 4 is greater than N = 3.
A client writes version 2. The coordinator sends it to all three replicas and waits for two acknowledgements.
Replicas 1 and 2 acknowledge. Replica 3 is slow. Two acknowledgements are enough, so the write succeeds while replica 3 still holds v1.
Now a read. It needs R = 2 answers. In the worst case the coordinator asks replicas 2 and 3: one has v2, one has v1.
The coordinator compares versions and returns the newest, v2. Any two replicas out of three must include at least one that holds the latest write, because 2 + 2 > 3.
With R = 1 instead, the coordinator could ask only replica 3 and return v1, a stale read. Because R + W = 3 is not greater than N, no overlap is guaranteed. That is the price of the faster read.
